chapter: The band, its players and singers
title: A happy sound, Ellington's 'Warm Valley' and happy blues
summary: Basie says he wants to be happy and play happy music, names Ellington's 'Warm Valley' as his favorite love song, and says he is happy when playing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Yes. I don't know whether they know it or not but they could give you their thinking of it. A lot of people could do that, but I can't. I won't try to. [I wouldn't be right yet,] You said you wanted a happy sound. Why happy?

I said why sad, I answered you. 'Cause That's the way I feel about it, want it happy. I want to be happy all the time and if there are certain kinds of music -- it is happy music. Now, you get a lot of great hits, an awful lot of hits that and they sold, but they're kind of sad sometimes too. There are some great lovesongs that have been written, which is great, the great standards, but I don't think that's happy.
My favorite love song is something that was written by Ellington, called Warm Valley. "That you play now," (Inaudible) Well, we've got it in the book.
It's merely for a feeling which I love,
because which I thought of him, it's beautiful.
And the blues, the blues are happy, your blues are happy, not sad. Happy blues.
I hope that's the way, that's the way I feel and that's the way I play it.
I understand you want to be happy, what if you don't feel happy and you're playing the blues. Do you play the blues according to how you feel at the time.
No. I'm not happy and want to be happy.
Would you say that there are times you're playing and you just aren't happy.
I don't know what time that is. I am happy when I am playing.
